ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p133/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p133/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p133/r1.claim: The Day destroys the world and raises people; Hell awaits the rebellious, every deed is registered, and their punishment is the natural result of what they did.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p133/r1.anchor: Each will face the deeds he had sent forward and each and every deed of his will be written in a register.

NAHHAS:v5p127/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p127/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p127/r8.claim: Their return is to Hell; āba yaʾūbu means return, as a poem says the dead do not return.
NAHHAS:v5p127/r8.anchor: أي مرجعهم إليها وآب يؤوب رجع كما قال ( وكل ذي غيبة يئوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425#2/r18.claim: الطاغون means unbelievers, and المآب is the place of return.

JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r9.claim: Ṭāghī, ʿātī, and ʿādī all describe someone who exceeds the limit in disobedience.
JISHUMI:v10p7247#2/r9.anchor: والطاغي والعاتي والعادي سواء، وهو من جاوز الحد في العصيان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r9.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r9.claim: مآبا means a place to return to and an outcome.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r10.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r10.claim: مآبا means a home or dwelling.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r11.claim: The tyrants are those who exceed limits in religion through disbelief or in worldly life through injustice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p185/r11.anchor: والمراد بالطاغين من طغى في دينه بالكفر أو في دنياه بالظلم

ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r4.claim: Li-t-taghin can attach to mirsad, making Hell a lookout for rebels, or to ma'ab, making it the rebels' final place of return.
ELMALILI:78:14-30#2/r4.anchor: tuğyan edenler, azgınlık yapanlar için ki bu, “mirsâd”a da, “meâb”a da ta‘alluk edebilir

STUDYQURAN:78:21/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:78:21/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:78:21/r1.claim: Hell is where those who rebel against the truth are sent.
STUDYQURAN:78:21/r1.anchor: Hell is the place to which those who rebel against the truth are sent

TAB-FULL:v24p21/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p21/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p21/r1.claim: Hell is a return and dwelling place for those who transgressed God’s limits in worldly life out of arrogance toward their Lord.
TAB-FULL:v24p21/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {للطاغين مآبا} [النبأ: 22] أي منزلا ومأوى

TAB-FULL:v24p21/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p21/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p21/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses maʾāban as a dwelling and refuge.
TAB-FULL:v24p21/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {للطاغين مآبا} [النبأ: 22] أي منزلا ومأوى

TAB-FULL:v24p21/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p21/r3.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v24p21/r3.claim: Sufyān glosses maʾāban as a return and dwelling place.

TABATABAI:78:21-23/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r8.claim: The tyrants are those characterized by ṭughyān, going beyond the proper limit.
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r8.anchor: الطاغون الملتبسون بالطغيان وهو الخروج عن الحد

TABATABAI:78:21-23/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r9.claim: Maʾāb is a place of return, from awb, “to return.”
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r9.anchor: والمآب اسم مكان من الأوب بمعنى الرجوع

TABATABAI:78:21-23/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r10.claim: Hell is the tyrants' return because they prepared it as their dwelling in worldly life and return to it after leaving this world.
TABATABAI:78:21-23/r10.anchor: والعناية في عدها مآبا للطاغين أنهم هيأوها مأوى لأنفسهم وهم في الدنيا ثم إذا انقطعوا عن الدنيا آبوا ورجعوا إليها

TABRISI:78:21-24/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:78:21-24/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:78:21-24/r4.claim: The transgressors are those who crossed God's limits and rebelled against Him; Hell is their return and destination, as though their crimes had already placed them there.
TABRISI:78:21-24/r4.anchor: للذين جاوزوا حدود الله وطغوا في معصية الله مرجعا يرجعون إليه ومصيرا فكأنه المجرم قد كان بإجرامه فيها

BURSEVI:v10p233/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p233/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p233/r3.claim: للطاغين may modify an omitted noun as an adjective of مرصادا, with مآبا in apposition; alternatively it may be a fronted circumstantial predicate of مآبا.
BURSEVI:v10p233/r3.anchor: ممتعلق بمضمر هو أما نعت لمرصادا

BURSEVI:v10p233/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p233/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p233/r4.claim: A طاغٍ exceeds the limit in disobedience, transgressing in religion through unbelief and in worldly life through oppression.
BURSEVI:v10p233/r4.anchor: قالوا الطاغي من طغى في دينه بالكفر وفي دنياه بالظلم وهو في اللغة من جاوز الحد في العصيان

BURSEVI:v10p233/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p233/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p233/r5.claim: Here the transgressors are polytheists, as the following verses indicate.
BURSEVI:v10p233/r5.anchor: والمراد هنا المشركون لما دل عليه ما بعده من الآيات

BURSEVI:v10p233/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p233/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p233/r6.claim: The destination is a return to which they will inevitably come; their punishment continues without end, unlike the finite punishment of a sinful believer.
BURSEVI:v10p233/r6.anchor: أي مرجعا يرجعون إليه لا محالة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil identify the transgressors as misguided polytheists.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p126#4/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬5)، ومقاتل (¬6): يريد للمشركين الضالين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:78:21-23/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:78:21-23/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:78:21-23/r2.claim: “The transgressors” means the disbelievers; Hell is their return.

QASHANI:78:19-22/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:78:19-22/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:78:19-22/r5.claim: For the wicked, Hell is their destination, as also stated in 19:72.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r4.claim: One Quranic sense is deviation or error, including the Companion’s denial that he made his associate transgress and the destination prepared for the transgressors.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الطغيان في القرآن على أربعة أوجه . أحدها : الضلال

SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r1.claim: للطاغين may modify مرصادا as an adjective, or be a circumstantial accusative from مآبا, understood as having been its adjective before being fronted; both analyses attach it to an omitted element.
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون صفة لمرصادا، وأن يكون حالا من " مآبا " كان صفته فلما تقدم نصب على الحال. وعلى هذين الوجهين فيتعلق بمحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r2.claim: Alternatively, للطاغين may attach directly to مرصادا or to مآبا, since مآبا means a place of return.
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون متعلقا بنفس " مرصادا " أو بنفس " مآبا " لأنه بمعنى مرجع

SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r3.speaker: ابن يعمر وأبو عمرو المنقري
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r3.claim: Ibn Ya'mur and Abu Amr al-Minqari read أن جهنم with أن opened; al-Zamakhshari construes it as giving the reason for the Hour and requital.
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن يعمر وأبو عمرو المنقري " أن جهنم " بفتح " أن ". قال الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the opened أن as making the Hour's establishment serve the purpose of requital, since Hell is a watch-post for transgressors.
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r4.anchor: على تعليل قيام الساعة بأن جهنم كانت مرصادا للطاغين، كأنه قيل: كان ذلك لإقامة الجزاء

SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r5.speaker: أبو عياض
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r5.claim: Abu Iyad reads في الصور with a fatḥa on the waw; the author says a similar reading was mentioned earlier.
SAMIN-DURR:78:22/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عياض " في الصور " بفتح الواو. وتقدم مثله

ZAJJAJ:v5p273/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p273/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p273/r3.claim: Maʾāb means the place to which the transgressors return.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r1.claim: The transgressors are those who exceed the limits in rebellion.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r2.claim: Alusi gives several parses: the fronted phrase may modify an omitted description of mirṣād or be a fronted circumstantial of maʾāb; it may also be a second predicate or attach to either noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r2.anchor: متعلق بمضمر أما نعت لمرصادا أي كائنا للطاغين وأما حال من قوله تعالى مآبا قدم عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r3.claim: Maʾāb may substitute for mirṣād, serve as a second predicate, or describe mirṣād; li-l-ṭāghīn may attach to it or be its circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r3.anchor: مآبا قيل بدل من مرصادا على جميع الأوجه بدل كل من كل وقيل هو ثان لكانت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r4.claim: If mirṣād is understood as prepared for them, the phrase uses the sense of arṣadtu, ‘I prepared for him.’
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r4.anchor: وعليه قيل معنى مرصادرا لهم معدة لهم من قولهم أرصدت له أي أعددت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr, al-Minqari, and Ibn Yaʿmar read the hamza of an as open, supplying a causal preposition: this is for establishing the Hour’s recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمر والمنقري وابن يعمر أن جهنم بفتح الهمزة بتقدير لام جر لتعليل قيام الساعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r6.claim: Alusi questions the proposed explanation: the phrase about the pious should then also take an open hamza and be coordinated, while the suggestion that each reward independently demands the Hour does not explain establishing recompense itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p14#2/r6.anchor: بأنه ينبغي حينئذ أن يكون أن للمتقين أيضا بالفتح ومعطوفا على ما هنا لأنه بكليهما يتم التعليل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r6.claim: Here the transgressors are the disbelievers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p314/r7.claim: Maʾāb means a place of return to which they go back.

BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:19-23/r9.claim: For the rebels, Hell is a return and dwelling place.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r12.claim: Because averting harm takes priority over gaining benefit, the fearful destination is presented first.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r12.anchor: ولما كان درء المفاسد أولى من جلب المصالح , قدم ذكر المخوف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r13.claim: The ṭāghīn are those who exceed God's bounds.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r14.claim: Maʾāb means a return and abode: people were created for it, then prepared to depart through their primordial nature, revealed books, and messengers, before their denial brings them back.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p300/r14.anchor: أي مرجعا ومأوى بعد أن كان الله ذرأهم لها فكأنهم كانوا فيها

DURR-FULL:v8p394/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p394/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p394/r2.claim: Qatadah glosses maʾāban as a dwelling and place of return.
DURR-FULL:v8p394/r2.anchor: {للطاغين مآبا} قال: مأوى ومنزلا {لابثين فيها أحقابا}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r6.claim: Calling them the rebellious instead of using a pronoun brands them with their defining transgression.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p33/r6.anchor: والتعبير ب ( الطاغين ) إظهار في مقام الإضمار للتسجيل عليهم بوصف الطغيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r6.claim: The omitted complement of mirsad is supplied by maʾaban: it is a watch-post for the rebellious. This is best because the short verse cola allow a pause after mirsad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r6.anchor: والتقدير : مرصادا للطاغين ، وهذا أحسن لأن قرائن السورة قصار فيحسن الوقف عند { مرصادا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r7.claim: Other parses attach lil-taghin to mirsad and infer the complement of maʾaban, or let lil-taghin depend on both terms; neither alternative creates a semantic obstacle.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r7.anchor: ولك أن تجعل { للطاغين } متعلقا ب { مرصادا } وتجعل متعلق { مئابا } مقدرا دل عليه { للطاغين }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r9.claim: Maʾab is originally a place of return, transferred by metonymy to a dwelling and now commonly used for a place of residence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p35/r9.anchor: و { مئابا } : مكان الأوب وهو الرجوع ، أطلق على المقر والمسكن إطلاقا أصله كناية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r1.claim: Maʾaban can be a circumstantial predicate of Hell, a second predicate of kana, or an appositional specification of mirsad, since surveillance includes the destination of those watched.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r1.anchor: ونصب { مئابا } على الحال من { جهنم } أو على أنه خبر ثان لفعل { كانت } أو على أنه بدل اشتمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r2.claim: Lil-taghin most aptly modifies maʾaban and is brought forward to frighten the polytheists with their destination; attachment to mirsad or shared attachment is also possible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r2.anchor: و { للطاغين } متعلق ب { مئابا } قدم عليه لإدخال الروع على المشركين الذين بشركهم طغوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r3.claim: Taghyan is exceeding bounds through disregard for others' rights and arrogance; the definite form refers to the polytheists addressed as coming in companies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r3.anchor: والطغيان : تجاوز الحد في عدم الاكتراث بحق الغير والكبر ، والتعريف فيه للعهد فالمراد به المشركون المخاطبون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r4.claim: Explicitly naming the rebellious explains their punishment: shirk is the greatest transgression, turning from God's worship and arrogantly refusing His Messenger's call; the sura identifies them in 78:27–28.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r4.anchor: لأن الشرك أقصى الطغيان إذ المشركون بالله أعرضوا عن عبادته ومتكبرون على رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r5.claim: Muslims who slight God's rights or transgress against people contemptuously share in this warning in proportion to their resemblance to disbelievers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p36/r5.anchor: هذا وأن المسلمين المستخفين بحقوق الله ، أو المعتدين على الناس بغير حق ، واحتقارا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r3.claim: Opening with Hell explains the later word mafazan as Paradise, a place of triumph for the God-fearing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r3.anchor: فكان للابتداء بذكر جهنم ما يفسر المفاز في قوله ) إن للمتقين مفازا ( أنه الجنة لأن الجنة مكان فوز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r6.claim: These several readings depend on the exact order of Hell, mafazan, the overflowing cup, and the no-speech clause; the sequence makes meanings available that a different order would not.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r6.anchor: وهذه المعاني لا يتأتى جميعها إلا بجمل كثيرة لو لم يقدم ذكر جهنم ولم يعقب بكلمة ) مفازا ( . ولم يؤخر ) وكأسا دهاقا (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r7.claim: Rhetorical choices must be explained by the occasion and audience of revelation; reading only the local words can make interpreters force strained explanations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p110/r7.anchor: ذلك لأنه لم يلتفت إلا إلى مواقع ألفاظ الآية ، في حال أن مقتضياتها في الواقع منوطة بالمقامات التي نزلت فيها الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#7/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#7/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#7/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the transgressors as polytheists.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#7/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#7/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7#7/r2.claim: Maʾāb means a place of return.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r4.claim: The transgressors are rebellious sinners who oppose the messengers.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r5.claim: Ma'ab means a return, destination, final turning place, or resting place.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say no one enters Paradise without crossing the Fire: one with a pass is saved, while the rest are detained.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p305/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن، وقتادة في قوله: {إن جهنم كانت مرصادا} يعني: أنه لا يدخل أحد الجنة حتى يجتاز بالنار،

MUQATIL:78:20-29/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:78:20-29/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:78:20-29/r3.claim: The transgressors are unbelievers, and their return is to Hell; the verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
MUQATIL:78:20-29/r3.anchor: يعني الكافرين { مآبا } [آية: 22] يعني المشركين مرجعا إليها

MUQATIL:78:20-29/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:78:20-29/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:78:20-29/r4.claim: Muqatil reports that this passage was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
MUQATIL:78:20-29/r4.anchor: يعني المشركين مرجعا إليها نزلتفي الوليد بن المغيرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p311#4/r1.claim: The transgressors are the disbelievers, for whom Hell is the place of return.

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r13.claim: Lit-tāghīn maʾāb is an appositive to marṣād; maʾāb means return, from āba yaʾūbu.

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r14.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r14.claim: Qatada glosses maʾāb as a refuge or dwelling.

QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r15.claim: The transgressors are those who transgress in religion through unbelief or in worldly life through oppression.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:21-25/r15.anchor: والمراد بالطاغين من طغى في دينه بالكفر، أو في دنياه بالظلم
